HIGHLIGHTS + 


CAMP PERROT - GIRLS' CAMP 1954 


The camp was divided this year into two sections instead of the 
customary threes The Senior Section was composed of 6 tents of 
girls ranging in age from 13-16 and the Junior Section of 7 tents 

of girls between the ages of 10-12. The average tent consisted 

of 6 campers and their Counsellor with the Section Director having 

a tent in her own Section. There were a total of 91 girls attending 
camp during the two-week period which was 12 below the confortable 
capacitye 


The camp was completely divided into two tribes consisting of an 
equal number of Seniors, Juniors and Counsellors on eache The 
campers elected a Big Chief (Senior) and a Little Chief (Junior) 

of each tribe. These 4 campers accepted a great deal of responsib- 
ility in helping plan program and in stirring up enthusiasm amongst 
their tribes. The majority of activities were carrid on along the 
tribal basis - with points being awarded for such things as clean- 
up, passing of tests, etce The competition was always at a high 
level and the campers enjoyed the competitive spirit which existede 


The morning program each day was made up of swimming lessons 
and interest groups - the campers picked their own interest group 
or groups each day and Counsellors were assigned to aover these 
according to the number of campers who wanted the activity. The 
afternoon program was carried out either in section or tent groups 
with such acitivities as track meets and games being popular. 
Evening program was either sectional or all campe 


Puppet Show: Each tribe undertook, with the help of their 
Counsellors, to stage two puppet shows - one Senior and one Juniore 
They wrote the scrips, made the puppets, dressed them, painted the 
scenery and set up the staze.e This was a remarkable achievement on 
their part since it took them only 5 days and the plays themselves 
were excellent.e The program covered experience in dramatics, crafts, 
production and served to tie all these togethers The enthusiasm 
shown was wonderful and the campers were so pleased with the results 
they decided to stage the whole thing again the next day - Parents! 
Day . 

Sunday evenings: It was decided this year to try to have a serious 
and meaningful program on Sunday evenings - the campers chose thvir 
favorite hymns and these along with stories and poems and a camp- 
fire created an atmosphere which will long be remembered by 
counsellors as well as camperse This in addition to a Chapel Service 
in the morning made Sunday a little special at Perrote 


Other all camp programs included such things as Christmas Day, 
Indian Council, Junior, Senior Barn Dance, Amateur Night, Pirate 
and Sailor Day, 6%ce

FURTHER COMMENTS: 


After having been at Camp Perrot for only two weeks, I do not feel qualified 
to make t oo many recommendations or definite statements about the suitability of 
the campsite or the length of time devoted to boys and girls at the campe Whether 
this wasatypical year or not I cannot say, but from my observations, I feel I can 
make one or two commentse 


The girls' camp was not filled to capacitye Perhaps this year the consistent 
bad weather for the two months preceeding had something to do with ite If this 
situation is repeated perhaps the reasons are not so obvious = it would be well to 
consider that most girls' camps' registrations drop during the month of August - 
the nights are cold and parents often feel that this is not the best time to send 
children to campe Another reason which comes to mind is that difficulty in getting 
anyone to act as counsellor during the middle two weeks of August. lost available 
counsellor material has already been spoken for - and although I am grateful to those 
girls who helped this year, and although I know they tried hard and did their best 
for the campers, with few exceptions they just weren't good enoughe Camp Perrot has 
definite possibilities as far as girls’ camp is concerned, and I feel our program 
was fairly good but I know it could be a great deal better. 


Another thing which happened this summer which caused me a great deal of concern 
was the unheralded visit of a group of local boys into camp at about 3:00 Ad. 
During their first visit they had actually gone right into ome of the Senior tents 
and I believe only the quick thinking of a couple of counsellors saved the tent 
from panice The camp site is so completely open to the road that it invites that 
sort of thing meant only as a prank by a group of bored teen-age boys - but when 
13 and 14 year old girls go home and tell their parents of these happenings it 
wontt do the camp any good. 


Whether this situation is repeated or not, I think it advisable to have 
some sort of fence closing the property off from the road and a more adequate 
fence between the adjoining field and the camp. 


Another necessity for next summer is a cocoa-matting covering on the dock. 
The present canvas cover becomes extremely slippery when wet (which is most of 
the time) and there were several badfalls. We were fortunate that the injuries 
sustained on the dock were not seriouse 


Respectfully submitted, 
Jean Machane
